text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Nobel Peace laureate Jose Ramos Horta shows images of torture in East Timor to U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva.

- Shareholders of ship repairer Lisnave approved division of company into Lisnave-Estaleiros Navais, the operating arm, in which small investors will hold preference shares with no voting rights, and Gestnave, the human resources concern in which the government will hold a majority stake.

- Madeira and Azores may receive significantly more state funds if the agreement on the constitutional reform signed between the ruling Socialist Party and the opposition Social Democrat Party is approved by parliament.

- State rail company Caminhos de Ferro Portugues lost 72 billion escudos taking accumulated losses to 500 billion escudos. These figures will rise in the years to come due to the rising costs of on-going projects.
- Investment of 300 billion escudos will be made on roads in 1998 and a new financing system for them is possible, Planning Minister Joao Cravinho, said.

- State electricity company (EDP) will present profits of 81 billion escudos to shareholders on Tuesday, an increase of 21 percent compared with 1995. On Wednesday, it will ask the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to authorise its quotation on the New York stock market.
